title: Probability by Counting Outcomes
learning_objectives: Describe a sample space and events as Python data and predicates
Apply the complement and inclusion–exclusion rules
entry_point: two_dice(); probability(space, event); complement(space, event); union(space, a, b); independent(space, a, b)
hints: `[(d1, d2) for d1 in range(1, 7) for d2 in range(1, 7)]` builds the space in the right order.
`Fraction(sum(1 for o in space if event(o)), len(space))` is the probability.
The intersection event is `lambda o: a(o) and b(o)`.

failure_feedback.advice: Use two nested loops (or a nested comprehension) over 1..6, first die outer.
Subtract the probability of both events, which inclusion–exclusion counts twice.
Compare P(A and B) with P(A) * P(B) using Fractions.
Raise ValueError when the sample space is empty.
